title: Thought themes (content of automatic thoughts)
description: What automatic thoughts are about: the content themes that, under Beck's content-specificity hypothesis, characterize particular emotions and disorders. Tags the theme of automatic thoughts and hot thoughts in formulation slots. Each concept carries emotions (em ids of the emotions the theme typically drives) and conditions (topic values from _schema.md section 5). A theme is the content of in-the-moment thoughts; the matching enduring beliefs are in cb and ib. The suicide-relevant themes (hopelessness, burdensomeness, entrapment) are coded here, and rk links to them.
sources: Beck-1976 § Cognitive content of emotional disorders
Clark-Beck-2010 § Ch. 2 The Cognitive Model of Anxiety

concepts.label: Loss and defeat
concepts.definition: Thoughts that something valued has been lost or that one has been beaten or diminished: a person, role, status, health or goal.
concepts.client_wording: Thoughts about losing something or someone important, or feeling beaten down.
concepts.example: "Since the divorce, I've lost everything that mattered."

concepts.label: Inadequacy and failure
concepts.definition: Thoughts that one is incompetent, weak or not good enough to meet demands, and has failed or will fail.
concepts.client_wording: Thoughts that you're not capable or good enough, or that you keep failing.
concepts.example: "I can't do anything right at work."
sources: Beck-2021 § Ch. 17 Introduction to Beliefs (helpless core beliefs)

concepts.label: Abandonment and rejection
concepts.definition: Thoughts that one is unlovable or will be rejected, left or let down by the people one depends on.
concepts.client_wording: Thoughts that people you care about will leave you or don't really want you.
concepts.example: "He'll get bored of me and leave, like everyone else."
sources: Young-etal-2003 § Ch. 1 Schema Therapy: Conceptual Model (abandonment/instability)
Beck-2021 § Ch. 17 Introduction to Beliefs (unlovable core beliefs)

concepts.label: Hopelessness
concepts.definition: Thoughts that the future is bleak, problems will not improve and nothing one does will make a difference. A key suicide risk signal.
concepts.client_wording: Thoughts that things will never get better, no matter what you do.
concepts.example: "There's no point. It's always going to be like this."
sources: Beck-etal-2024 § Ch. 9 Treating the Suicidal Patient
Beck-etal-1985 § Abstract: Hopelessness Scale and eventual suicide

concepts.label: Perceived burdensomeness
concepts.definition: Thoughts that one is a liability to others and that they would be better off without one, often fused with self-hatred. Raises suicide risk.
concepts.client_wording: Thoughts that you're a burden and others would be better off without you.
concepts.example: "My family would be better off if I wasn't here."

concepts.label: Entrapment
concepts.definition: Thoughts that one is trapped in an intolerable situation or inner pain with no way out, often following defeat or humiliation.
concepts.client_wording: Feeling stuck in unbearable pain or circumstances with no way out.
concepts.example: "I can't escape this, and I can't keep living like this."
sources: OConnor-Kirtley-2018 § Motivational phase: defeat and entrapment

concepts.label: Threat and danger
concepts.definition: Thoughts that physical or psychological harm is likely or imminent in a situation; the core content of anxiety and fear.
concepts.client_wording: Thoughts that something dangerous or harmful is about to happen.
concepts.example: "Something bad will happen if I leave the house."
sources: Clark-Beck-2010 § Ch. 2 The Cognitive Model of Anxiety

concepts.label: Vulnerability
concepts.definition: Thoughts that one is weak, exposed or unable to protect oneself or cope with threat, and that help is unavailable.
concepts.client_wording: Thoughts that you couldn't protect yourself or cope if something went wrong.
concepts.example: "If something happens, I'll be on my own and helpless."
sources: Clark-Beck-2010 § Ch. 2 The Cognitive Model of Anxiety

concepts.label: Physical catastrophe
concepts.definition: Thoughts that bodily sensations signal an immediate disaster such as a heart attack, suffocation, fainting or collapse.
concepts.client_wording: Thoughts that a racing heart or dizziness means something terrible is happening right now.
concepts.example: "My heart is pounding. I'm having a heart attack."
sources: Clark-1986 § Catastrophic misinterpretation of bodily sensations

concepts.label: Serious illness
concepts.definition: Thoughts that benign symptoms or medical uncertainty mean one has, or will develop, a serious disease that has been missed.
concepts.client_wording: Thoughts that a symptom means you have a serious illness doctors have missed.
concepts.example: "This headache means I have a brain tumor."

concepts.label: Loss of control
concepts.definition: Thoughts that one will lose control of mind, body, emotions or behavior, for example going mad, acting on an impulse or being overwhelmed.
concepts.client_wording: Thoughts that you'll lose control, go crazy, or do something you can't stop.
concepts.example: "If this feeling gets any stronger, I'll lose my mind."
sources: Clark-1986 § Catastrophic misinterpretation of bodily sensations

concepts.label: Negative evaluation
concepts.definition: Thoughts that others are noticing and judging one negatively, that one will appear anxious, awkward or inadequate and lose status or acceptance.
concepts.client_wording: Thoughts that people are judging you and will think badly of you.
concepts.example: "They can see I'm blushing. They'll think I'm weird."

concepts.label: Sleep loss and its consequences
concepts.definition: Thoughts that one will not sleep and that poor sleep will seriously harm health, mood or next-day functioning.
concepts.client_wording: Thoughts that you won't sleep and that tomorrow, or your health, will be ruined.
concepts.example: "If I don't fall asleep now, I'll fall apart at work tomorrow."
sources: Harvey-2002 § Excessive negatively toned cognitive activity

concepts.label: Contamination
concepts.definition: Thoughts that one is or will become dirty, infected or polluted through contact with substances, places or people, and may spread harm.
concepts.client_wording: Thoughts that you're dirty or infected, or could spread germs or harm.
concepts.example: "I touched the door handle. Now I'll make my kids sick."

concepts.label: Inflated responsibility for harm
concepts.definition: Thoughts whose content is being to blame for possible harm: that one could cause it, must prevent it, and failing to act equals causing it.
concepts.client_wording: Thoughts that it's up to you to stop anything bad happening, and it's your fault if it does.
concepts.example: "If I don't check the stove again and there's a fire, it'll be my fault."

concepts.label: Significance of thoughts
concepts.definition: Thoughts whose content is that one's intrusive or uncontrolled thoughts are meaningful, dangerous or revealing of one's character, and must be controlled.
concepts.client_wording: Thoughts that having an upsetting thought means something bad about you or is dangerous.
concepts.example: "Having this thought about hurting my baby means I'm a monster."
sources: OCCWG-1997 § Overimportance and control of thoughts

concepts.label: Violation and unfairness
concepts.definition: Thoughts that one has been wronged, treated unfairly, disrespected or had important rules broken by others, often seen as intentional.
concepts.client_wording: Thoughts that someone treated you unfairly or broke the rules on purpose.
concepts.example: "She deliberately humiliated me in front of everyone."
sources: Greenberger-Padesky-2016 § Ch. 15 Understanding Your Anger, Guilt, and Shame

concepts.label: Transgression
concepts.definition: Thoughts that one has done something wrong, broken one's own moral code or hurt someone, focused on the act rather than the whole self.
concepts.client_wording: Thoughts that you did something wrong or hurt someone and should have acted differently.
concepts.example: "I snapped at my daughter. That was a terrible thing to do."
sources: Greenberger-Padesky-2016 § Ch. 15 Understanding Your Anger, Guilt, and Shame

concepts.label: Defect and exposure
concepts.definition: Thoughts that the self is fundamentally flawed, bad or unacceptable, and that others will discover it and reject or humiliate one.
concepts.client_wording: Thoughts that something is deeply wrong with you and people will find out.
concepts.example: "If they knew the real me, they'd be disgusted."
sources: Greenberger-Padesky-2016 § Ch. 15 Understanding Your Anger, Guilt, and Shame
Young-etal-2003 § Ch. 1 Schema Therapy: Conceptual Model (defectiveness/shame)

concepts.label: Permanent damage after trauma
concepts.definition: Thoughts after trauma that one has been permanently damaged or changed, and that one's life, body or future is ruined beyond recovery.
concepts.client_wording: Thoughts that what happened has changed or damaged you for good.
concepts.example: "I'll never be the person I was. He ruined my life."
sources: Ehlers-Clark-2000 § Negative appraisals of the trauma and its sequelae
Beierl-etal-2020 § Negative appraisals and perceived permanent change

concepts.label: Shape, weight and eating control
concepts.definition: Thoughts that one looks fat, has gained weight, has eaten too much or lost control over eating, and must restrict or compensate.
concepts.client_wording: Thoughts that you look fat, ate too much or lost control, and need to make up for it.
concepts.example: "I've eaten far too much. I look huge. I have to skip dinner."
sources: Fairburn-2008 § Ch. 8 Shape Concern, Shape Checking, Feeling Fat and Mindsets

concepts.label: Appearance defect
concepts.definition: Thoughts that a specific feature of one's appearance is defective or ugly, is noticed by others and is central to one's worth.
concepts.client_wording: Thoughts that part of how you look is ugly or wrong and others notice it.
concepts.example: "Everyone is staring at my nose. It's hideous."
sources: Veale-2004 § Cognitive behavioural model of body dysmorphic disorder

concepts.label: Persecution
concepts.definition: Thoughts that others intend to cause one harm, physical, psychological or social, now or in the future.
concepts.client_wording: Thoughts that other people are deliberately out to harm you.
concepts.example: "My neighbors are plotting to get rid of me."

concepts.label: Personal gain and grandiosity
concepts.definition: Inflated thoughts about one's abilities, importance and prospects, overestimating gains and underestimating risks; typical of hypomania and mania.
concepts.client_wording: Thoughts that you're unstoppable, special or certain to succeed, so risks don't matter.
concepts.example: "I've had a brilliant idea. I'll make a fortune and nothing can go wrong."
sources: Mansell-etal-2007 § Extreme appraisals of internal states
